Subject: Proposed MAP & evaluation timeline for Redwood pilot

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great discussion. Per our call, I put together a short Mutual Action Plan (attached) that maps the commercial milestones to the evaluation steps so we can align on a target close date. High-level proposal:

- Evaluation window: 4 weeks (Mar 15–Apr 12) with two checkpoints (end of week 2 and final demo)
- Production pilot (post-eval): 3-month ramp
- Commercial ask: initial committed throughput for month 1 = 100k tokens/day, ramping to 500k tokens/day by month 3
- Discount profile: 10% on list for committed monthly throughput; additional 5% if 6-month renewal executed within pilot

Key outstanding commercial questions I want to surface now so we can address them in the MAP: pricing true-ups (how we account for overage), price protection (term length for protected rates), and a clean definition of "billable usage" (API calls vs. tokens vs. active user). Our legal team flagged a couple of redline points that affect economics — I'll loop them in once we have your procurement team's preferred language.

I attached Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx with the milestone dates and a proposed milestone-based payment schedule. Can you confirm the evaluation acceptance criteria (SLA, latency targets, specific success metrics) by next Tue 3/9 so our engineering team can prioritize the test harness?

If the MAP looks OK, we can attach a Statement of Work and run a short SOW redline pass concurrently with procurement.

Regards,

Quick notes from engineering on how we'll run the evaluation:

- Test harness: we'll provide a reproducible benchmark toolkit and a sample traffic generator that can be run inside your staging environment.
- Acceptance criteria (proposal): median latency <= 200ms for 512-token request, 99th <= 700ms; inference success rate >= 98% for the target prompts provided.
- Data handling: KV cache will be ephemeral; results won't be retained beyond evaluation unless explicitly enabled.

On commercial mechanics:
- True-ups: our standard is monthly reconciliation with a 30-day notice on adjustments. We can consider a tolerance band (e.g., +/- 10%) before a monetary true-up applies.
- Price protection: we can offer a 12-month rate lock on any committed pricing line items for the initial contract term.
- Usage definition: we typically bill by tokens (consumed model tokens plus prompt tokens). If you prefer per-API-call, we can translate to an equivalent token bucket in the SOW.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Draft SOW and initial commercial redlines

Forwarding initial SOW with redlines from our legal ops. High-level legal positions that affect economics:

1) True-ups: legal proposes a lookback reconciliation with a 60-day window and allows retrospective adjustments for underpayment. Commercial has asked to limit retrospective monetary adjustments to >10% variance. Need to resolve who owns audit costs.

2) Price protection: legal wants to tie price protection only to software unit prices; they did not want to lock third-party infra pass-throughs. Commercial earlier offered 12 months — confirm and state it in the fee schedule.

3) Definition of usage: legal prefers a broad definition "billable usage = API requests resulting in token consumption as measured at the platform ingress point." Acme requested per-API-call semantics. This difference changes overage math (API-call based caps are easier for procurement forecasting; token-based billing is tighter to unit economics).

4) True-up caps and credits: proposed language currently states: "If underreporting is identified, Redwood may invoice for underbilled usage less any good-faith adjustments; customer may dispute within 45 days." Acme procurement asked for a cap (e.g., limit retrospective bill to 6 months).

I've attached Draft_SOW_redlines.docx. I recommend we get Acme procurement's counsel into the thread once they have a preferred definition for billable usage so our counsel can redline accordingly.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
